target: AArch64 PCI QEMU, one guest CPU, current desktop ISO, disposable disk
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -netdev user,id=net0 -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0,disable-legacy=on' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-tosmisc-jukepuppet-current-2026-11-11.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-demo-system-context --demo-system-path /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSMisc.ZC --demo-system-module /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSConfig.ZC --demo-system-module /System/Gr/ScreenCast.ZC --demo-system-module /System/BlkDev/DiskCheck.ZC --demo-system-module /Apps/Psalmody/Load.ZC --demo-system-module /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSMisc.ZC
verified: TOSMisc default configuration, exact-font OCR over all 94 printable glyphs, dollar-sign document serialization, SoundShift/AUWrite round trip, GR2MV frame round trip, and ScreenCast GR/AU capture passed.
TOSMisc MemTest completed its data- and code-heap stress loops and returned to the compiler.
Psalmody Load.ZC loaded the stock JukePuppet implementation; the stock childish.ZC song fixture was listed and played through JukeSongsPuppet, which returned normally.
A Beep fixture was listed, executed by JukePuppet, entered its looping Song body, and was stopped by the normal puppet cleanup path.
The graphical terminal recovered, accepted 40+2 as 42, and final zstatus reported failed=0.
remaining: DiskCheckAll requires the configured C:/D: drive workflow; the ARM64 bridge still lacks the stock writable C: and RAM B: drives.
TOSDistro standard image generation and other drive-copy/format operations remain blocked on real writable multi-volume semantics.
The Beep fixture check establishes song execution and cleanup, not captured or audible QEMU audio output.
Live UTM and physical Pi 4B acceptance were not performed by this run.
scope_note: Non-destructive QEMU runtime evidence using a disposable guest disk. TOSMisc and JukePuppet remain partial at the wider drive-workflow scope; these checks do not claim configured writable-drive, full filesystem or distribution-builder acceptance.
